title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 2: praescientia practica / scientia approbationis — Catharinus
pass_a_gloss: But let us weigh the very words a little more carefully. The Apostle did not say, whom he foresaw; but, whom he foreknew, οὓς προέγνω. Now this foreknowledge is practical, not intuitive: and it is called by the theologians the knowledge of approbation. The sense therefore is: Whom God loved, and by his eternal good pleasure separated from others and approved, those he predestinated, &c. Nothing is more usual in the Scriptures than that to know or to cognize is put for to love or to approve; as not to know for to hate and to disapprove. I never knew you, Matt. vii. 23. The Lord knoweth the way of the righteous, Ps. i. 6. Hence Catharinus on this very place: What is that he foreknew, except that he foreloved?
pass_b_english: Weigh the words more closely. Paul did not say "whom he foresaw," but "whom he foreknew" (οὓς προέγνω). This foreknowledge is practical, not bare intuition — what theologians call the knowledge of approbation. Sense: those God loved and, by his eternal good pleasure, set apart from others and approved — those he predestined. Scripture often uses "know" for love or approval, and "not know" for hate or rejection ("I never knew you," Matt. 7:23; "The Lord knows the way of the righteous," Ps. 1:6). So Catharinus on this place: What is "he foreknew," if not "he foreloved"?
source_text: Sed ipsa verba expendamus paulo accuratius. Non dixit Apostolus, quos praevidit; sed, quos praescivit, οὓς προέγνω. At haec praescientia practica est, non intuitiva: & scientia approbationis vocatur a Theologis. Sensus igitur est; Quos Deus dilexit, & ab aeterno suo beneplacito secretos ab aliis comprobavit, hos praedestinavit, &c. Nihil usitatius in Scripturis quam ut scire sive cognoscere ponatur pro amare sive approbare; sicuti nescire pro odisse & improbare. Non novi vos, Matth. vii. 23. Novit Dominus viam justorum, Psal. i. 6. Hinc Catharinus in hunc ipsum locum, Quid est quod praescivit, nisi predilexit?
